The problem is not with the fzf itself, it's happening when I start the `:terminal`. To reproduce:

* Set in your .vimrc the following `autocmd`:
```
  augroup StartTerminalInInsertMode
    " https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/8816
    autocmd!
    autocmd TermOpen term://* startinsert
  augroup END
```
* Write 4000 chars in the buffer and start the terminal (`4000ia<esc>:terminal`).

It will crash with segment fault.

Hi, @blueyed.

There is no problem at all when the command is `nvim -u NONE`. You need a minimum set of config to simulate that. Sorry for not making this clear in the message above.

To simulate that:

1. Set your `.vimrc` with the commands below:
```
set hidden
set nowrap

augroup StartTerminalInInsertMode
  " https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/8816
  autocmd!
  autocmd TermOpen term://* startinsert
augroup END
```

2. Start nvim with `nvim --noplugin`.
3. Write 4000 chars in the buffer and start the terminal (`4000ia<esc>:terminal`).

body: @dm1try Thank you for debugging! When I thought about it, the `term_attrs` are all initialized to zero. Therefore, the part of `linebuf_attr` that exceeds the width of the terminal will be zero. Also, the part that exceeds the `term_attrs` should be fine by assigning zero (no attribute). I fixed it with that idea.
